Front: What is the main purpose of `javac` and what is its basic command format?
Back: `javac` is the Java compiler that translates human-readable source code (`.java` files) into platform-independent bytecode (`.class` files). Command format: `javac [options] [sourcefiles]`
Extra: Example: `javac -d bin src/com/example/App.java` compiles the source file and outputs the compiled class to the `bin/` directory.

Front: What common syntax/naming mistakes should you avoid when using the `javac` compiler command?
Back: 1. Do not pass the `.class` extension (e.g. `javac App.class` is wrong; use `javac App.java`).\n2. Do not omit the `.java` extension entirely (e.g. `javac App` is wrong and yields an annotation processing error).
Code: $ javac App\nerror: Class names, 'App', are only accepted if annotation processing is explicitly requested

Front: What is the purpose of the `java` CLI command and how does it execute single-file source code (Java 11+)?
Back: The `java` command launches a JVM, loads a specified class, and executes its `main` method. Since Java 11, running `java App.java` directly compiles and executes the file in-memory without producing a physical `.class` file on disk.
Extra: Command examples:\n`java com.example.App` (runs class from classpath)\n`java App.java` (directly compiles and runs in memory)

Front: What is the structure and purpose of a `jar` (Java Archive) file?
Back: A JAR file is a ZIP-formatted archive that aggregates multiple `.class` files, resource files, and metadata (like a manifest) into a single file for easy distribution.
Extra:
You can view the contents of a JAR file using:
`jar -tf app.jar`
Or extract it using:
`jar -xf app.jar`
Since it is a ZIP archive, you can also rename it to `.zip` to extract it.

Front: What is the CLI command to create a basic JAR archive, and what do the flags `-c`, `-f`, and `-C` stand for?
Back:
Command: `jar -cf archive-name.jar -C class-dir .`
Flags:
`-c`: Create a new archive
`-f`: Specify the archive file name
`-C`: Change to the specified directory to add files, ensuring correct package subdirectories are preserved.
Extra: Example:\n`jar -cvf app.jar -C bin/ .`\nPackages everything inside the `bin/` directory without including the "bin/" prefix inside the JAR paths.

Front: What makes a JAR file "executable" and how do you run it?
Back: An executable JAR contains a Manifest file (`META-INF/MANIFEST.MF`) containing a `Main-Class` attribute defining the entry-point class with a `main` method. It is executed using: `java -jar app.jar`
Extra: Attempting to run a standard library JAR with `java -jar` yields:\n`no main manifest attribute, in library.jar`

Front: What is the `Classpath` and how do you specify it on different operating systems?
Back: The Classpath tells the Java compiler (`javac`) and runtime (`java`) where to look for user-defined classes and libraries. Specify it using `-cp` or `--class-path` with `:` as the path separator on Linux/macOS and `;` on Windows.

Front: What is the purpose of the JAR manifest file and where is it located?
Back: The Manifest file (`MANIFEST.MF`) is a text file containing key-value metadata configuring the JAR. It is located at `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` inside the archive.
Extra: Key attributes:\nNote: The file must end with a trailing blank newline, otherwise attributes may be ignored!

Front: What is Apache Maven and what is its configuration file?
Back: Apache Maven is a declarative project management and build automation tool that organizes builds, dependencies, and lifecycles based on a Project Object Model configured in `pom.xml`.
Extra:
Core commands:
`mvn clean compile` (compiles source files)
`mvn clean test` (runs tests)
`mvn clean package` (packages JAR)

Front: What is Gradle and how does its configuration differ from Maven?
Back: Gradle is a flexible build automation tool that uses Groovy or Kotlin DSL (Domain Specific Language) scripts (`build.gradle` or `build.gradle.kts`) instead of XML, allowing programmable and highly customizable build tasks.
Extra: Command to build a Gradle project:\n`gradle clean build`\nGradle resolves dependencies transitively and caches them similarly to Maven.

Front: What is a dependency conflict ("Jar Hell") and how do build tools help resolve it?
Back: Dependency conflict happens when two transitively pulled libraries require different, incompatible versions of the same dependency. Build tools resolve it using conflict resolution policies (Maven defaults to "nearest definition" in dependency tree; Gradle defaults to "newest version").

Front: Describe the standard Maven/Gradle project directory structure for Java source files and resources.
Back:
`src/main/java/`: Production Java source files
`src/main/resources/`: Production properties, configuration, and asset files
`src/test/java/`: JUnit test source files
`src/test/resources/`: Test-only configuration and mock data files.
Extra: Example path: `src/main/java/com/example/App.java`\nIf production resources are placed in `src/main/java` by mistake, they might not be packaged into the JAR, causing runtime file-loading errors.

Front: What is a unit test in JUnit, and what are two common assertion pitfalls to avoid?
Back: A unit test is a method annotated with `@Test` that checks the correctness of a small piece of code. Pitfalls:\n1. Forgetting `@Test` annotation (method is silently ignored).\n2. Swapping argument order: `assertEquals(actual, expected)` (should be `expected` first, then `actual`).
